title: merge-forecast: match each ticket's scope once per run, not once per pair
body:
Make `merge-forecast` much faster without changing any output. Spec: `.adlc/specs/merge-forecast-scope-index.md` (read it first; it is the contract).

Why: `merge-forecast --json` takes 7.8 s on a 10-ticket, ~10,000-file repository and 36 s on average in real sessions. A CPU profile puts 77% of it in `globMatch` (`packages/core/lib/glob.mjs`). `globMatch` is fine; merge-forecast calls it far too often. In `packages/merge-forecast/lib/signals.mjs`, `signalNamespaceRoutes`, `signalMigrationCollision`, `signalGraphCoupling`, `signalCoChange` and `importRadiusIntersects` each recompute `repoFiles.filter((f) => scope.some((g) => globMatch(g, f)))` for both tickets of EVERY pair (3 to 5 times per pair side), and `lib/forecast.mjs` does it again in the zero-match validation.

What to build:
1. New file `packages/merge-forecast/lib/scope-index.mjs` exporting `compileGlob(pattern)` and `createScopeIndex(repoFiles)`, exactly as the spec's Design section describes. `compileGlob` handles a literal pattern with `===` and `literal**` with `startsWith`; for every other pattern it rejects on cheap necessary conditions (leading literal prefix, trailing literal suffix, minimum length) and otherwise returns `globMatch(pattern, path)` from `@adlc/core`. It never re-implements the matcher. A non-string pattern compiles to a matcher that calls `globMatch` on every call. `createScopeIndex` exposes `files(scope)`, `filesNormalized(scope)`, `matcher(scope)` (a predicate built once per scope content, never throwing when built) and `matches(scope, path)`, caches by scope content (JSON of an all-string array), and sends any scope that is not an array of strings through the shared old expression `(scope ?? []).some(...)` (same throw cases and error type).
2. `lib/forecast.mjs`: build one index right after `walkTree`, use it for the zero-match validation, pass it to `pairScore` as `opts.scopeIndex`.
3. `lib/signals.mjs`: `pairScore` passes `opts.scopeIndex` to every signal; each exported signal takes it as a new optional LAST parameter and builds a throwaway index when it is absent, so existing callers keep working. `importRadiusIntersects` uses `filesNormalized` for the importing side and one `matcher`, built before the loop, for the resolved candidates.
4. A benchmark, `packages/merge-forecast/test/bench/scope-index.bench.mjs` (under test/ so the mutation gate treats it as test tooling), that runs offline on a synthetic corpus (10,000 files, 10 tickets, one with 108 globs), checks the old filtering and the index agree, prints both timings plus an end-to-end `runForecast` timing, and with `--forecast <path>` compares against another implementation.
5. A short README note on performance.

Do NOT touch `packages/core` (glob.mjs is generated source copied into rail-enforcing hooks) or any other package. Do not edit the rails.

Acceptance (each has a command; numbering follows the spec):
- AC1-AC4 scope-index contract: `node --test packages/merge-forecast/test/scope-index.test.mjs` passes.
- AC5 every signal uses the index it is given: `node --test packages/merge-forecast/test/scope-index-wiring.test.mjs` passes.
- AC6 forecast unchanged (library result and CLI `--json` bytes vs goldens recorded before the change): `node --test packages/merge-forecast/test/forecast-unchanged.test.mjs` passes.
- AC7 existing suite, on Node 18 and current: `node --test packages/merge-forecast/test/*.test.mjs` passes.
- AC8 offline benchmark: `node packages/merge-forecast/test/bench/scope-index.bench.mjs --forecast <dir>/packages/merge-forecast/lib/forecast.mjs` exits 0, with origin/main extracted to <dir> by `git archive origin/main packages/merge-forecast | tar -x -C <dir>` and `ln -s $PWD/node_modules <dir>/node_modules`.
- AC9 real data: the reference repository is a checkout of mentimeter/adlc at commit d01b1f6c (10 active tickets, 9,967 files; any repository with an .adlc ticket store and git history works the same way). From its root, `node <dir>/packages/merge-forecast/bin/merge-forecast.mjs --json > before.json` and `node <this-worktree>/packages/merge-forecast/bin/merge-forecast.mjs --json > after.json` give the same `shasum` and the same exit code, and the wall time drops.
- AC10 gates: `npm run preflight` exits 0.
acceptance: packages/merge-forecast/lib/scope-index.mjs exports compileGlob and createScopeIndex; compileGlob(p)(x) === globMatch(p, x) over a generated corpus of more than 100,000 pattern x path pairs, and the index (files, filesNormalized, matcher, matches) returns exactly the old filter results (order and duplicates kept), caches by scope content, keeps the old throw cases for odd scopes, and is the index every signal actually uses.
runForecast and merge-forecast --json produce output identical to goldens recorded before the change on a fixture that fires every signal; the existing merge-forecast suite still passes.
An offline benchmark shows the speed-up on a synthetic corpus, and a real-repository run prints byte-identical JSON with the same exit code, much faster.
